Sign in to a CryptPad account by its email and login-block secret. In CryptPad the server never sees a password — ownership is proven by an Ed25519 signature the client makes; this world represents that by the account existing. Every account-scoped tool (pins, uploads, admin) resolves the acting account from this session. Fails if no account has that email and secret.

email.description: The account email to sign in with.

content.description: The account secret (encrypted login-block content) to verify ownership with.

guards.auth: That account does not exist; sign in with a registered login block id.

_evidence.ref_code: Account ownership in CryptPad is an Ed25519 signature verification over the login block (Nacl.sign.detached.verify). The signature check cannot be modelled (the runtime cannot verify signatures), so the login is represented by the account existing; the opening session makes it the $actor for every scoped tool.
_evidence._note: auth wall is a real semantic (no such account) promoted to the auth wall; not evidence of a code precondition.

summary: CryptPad is a self-hosted, filesystem-backed, end-to-end-encrypted collaborative office suite: pads (channels) store encrypted messages and per-channel metadata (owners, restricted allow-lists, mailboxes), user accounts are encrypted login blocks protected by optional TOTP 2FA with per-account sessions, file uploads stage (BlobStage) then promote to owned Blobs with activity tracking, users pin channels into append-only per-user PinLogs, invitations and moderators are flat-file records, and scheduled expiry Tasks plus admin config Decrees persist to ndjson logs; admins operate over all of it via a single ADMIN RPC.
